name: St. Louis Landing Building C
headline: Building C at the Town of Fraser's St. Louis Landing is a new 70-unit, all-electric apartment building for households at 80% to 120% AMI, owned through the Fraser Housing Authority. It won $1,542,722 in 2025 Middle-Income Housing Tax Credits from CHFA in the program's first round.
why_it_matters: It is one of the first three MIHTC deals in Colorado and a test of a town-led model: the town bought the land with a state grant, the housing authority owns the building, and a turnkey developer builds it with bonds, Prop 123 equity, MIHTC and local funds. Building C was due to finish in November 2026, with first move-ins in December.

status.label: Under construction; first move-ins targeted December 2026
status.detail: Sky-Hi News reported that foundation work on Building C began in early August 2025, that the building was vertical in April 2026, and on 2026-09-29 that it would be done in November, with applications opening in early October and move-ins in early December 2026. The closings of the housing authority bonds and the MIHTC transfer have not been confirmed by a public record.

next_step: Watch for the certificate of occupancy and lease-up of Building C in November and December 2026, and the MIHTC certificate transfer, which is meant to fund at stabilization.

key_numbers.meaning: 27 studios, 35 one-bedrooms and 8 two-bedrooms at 80%, 100% and 120% AMI (application average 94.3% AMI).
State middle-income credit; Sky-Hi reports it runs for five years. The developer put the net value at about $5M.
Part of a three-building first phase (Buildings C, D and E, 129 units). Sky-Hi reported a total of about $75M in April 2026 and a $71.9M budget in September 2026.
Building C was to be finished in November 2026; Building E in spring 2027 and Building D in December 2027.

facts.value: 123 Edna Tucker Way, Fraser, CO 80442 (north side of Fraser near U.S. 40 and Grand County Road 8)
I/F, N: individuals and families, new construction
One four-story, wood-frame, elevator building of about 46,000 sq ft. It is all-electric, built to NGBS Bronze and solar-ready, with about 150 kW of roof solar priced as an option
The Lift free bus stops about 100 feet away; the Fraser/Winter Park Amtrak station is 0.2 miles away
Town deed restrictions limit renters to people working 30+ hours a week in Grand County; no remote workers and no short-term rentals
First phase of a two-phase St. Louis Landing master plan (former Victoria Village site), with an early childhood education center in Building E

money.note: 2025 award. The award report labels the column 'MIHTC Amount Requested'. Sky-Hi reports a five-year credit. It is planned as a transferable certificate that funds at stabilization and is bridged by bonds.

money.source: Fraser Housing Authority tax-exempt revenue bonds
money.note: Planned in the application. In April 2026 the town was still awaiting a delayed $2.2M tied to the housing authority bonds and Prop 123 funding.
Low-interest. The commitment letter was signed 2026-03-09; CHFA told the developers the money would not be available until mid-May 2026.

money.source: CHFA Middle Income Access Program (MIAP) subordinate loan

money.amount: $1M upfront plus $250,000 a year for 15 years
money.note: The application says the $250,000 a year supports Building C operating costs, including bond costs. Sky-Hi reports the $1M upfront contribution.

money.source: State grants (DOLA and Division of Housing)
money.note: These include More Housing Now ($2M and $1.5M), Strong Communities ($3M) and EIAF ($1M for the early childhood center). Building C gets a portion of the More Housing Now grant.

money.note: The Town bought the land in 2022.

money.note: The Town has paid $2.9M of development costs and $2.5M in grant matches. A $2.9M Town loan balance was expected after closing; the developer hopes to retire it with a DOLA grant and New Markets Tax Credits.

background.text: The Town bought the former Victoria Village site in May 2022 for $3.8M; an Operation Turnkey grant from the Division of Housing later reimbursed 80% of the cost.

The Town approved a master plan in mid-2023 after four public open houses, then the Final Plat and Major Site Plan for phase one in late July 2024. Infrastructure work started in October 2024 (the Town says groundbreaking was November 2024). The Development Agreement with MAHD was signed in January 2025.

Phase one has three buildings: C (70 units for 80% to 120% AMI), D (with a property management office and commercial space) and E (with the early childhood education center). Together they hold 129 units averaging about 89% AMI, with a bridge over St. Louis Creek.
The plan changed from early talk of 30% to 80% AMI homes to first-phase rentals at 80% to 120% AMI, which drew local criticism in 2025 and again when maximum rents came out in September 2026.
The application commits to at least 40 years of affordability. The Town's project page says all St. Louis Landing units will be deed-restricted in perpetuity.
In response to the market study, 120% AMI rents were set below the maximum MIHTC rents. The application included an underwriting waiver request.
Foundation work on Building C began in early August 2025. At that time interior finishes were expected by January 2026; the target later moved to completion in November 2026.
Sky-Hi reported that an August 2025 town resolution makes the housing authority responsible for $45M in project costs, including reimbursement of pre-financing costs.
Missing Prop 123 money could have paused work at a cost of $125,000 to $150,000 a month, per an April 2026 developer presentation.
A temporary leasing website is live, and the Town received more than 150 interest emails by 2026-09-16. Applications were to open in early October 2026.

discrepancies.text: CHFA's award descriptions and the application put Building C at 80% to 120% AMI, while Sky-Hi News in January and September 2026 describes the units as serving 30% to 120% AMI.
CHFA's May 2025 applicant report lists the sponsor as Mountain Affordable Housing Development, while the July 2025 award report and award descriptions list the Fraser Housing Authority.

Sky-Hi News reported a phase-one total of about $75 million ($50 million construction plus $25 million other costs) in April 2026, but a $71.9 million budget in September 2026, which it says has not changed since the three-building plan was finalized.
Sky-Hi News refers to the owner as the Fraser Valley Housing Authority, while CHFA names the Fraser Housing Authority.
